key_insight: Intern-Atlas builds a methodological evolution graph that explicitly models how research methods emerge, adapt, and build on one another, turning papers into a structured, machine-actionable research infrastructure for both humans and AI agents.
problem_solved: Current research infrastructure is document-centric and only provides citation links, failing to capture structured relationships and lineage between methods — which prevents reliable discovery, comparison, composition, and automated use by AI research agents.
method: Create a graph representation where nodes encode methods/components (algorithms, datasets, protocols, metrics) and directed edges encode derivation, adaptation, and dependency relationships.
Automatically extract candidate nodes and edges from papers, code, and metadata using NLP and code-analysis pipelines, augmented with human-in-the-loop curation to ensure precision.
Expose APIs and visualization tools for querying, traversing, and composing methodological lineages, enabling programmatic consumption by research agents and interactive exploration by scientists.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and research agents with a navigable, machine-readable map of methodological lineage that accelerates discovery, improves reproducibility, and enables automated method synthesis and adaptation.
visual_elements: A directed network diagram showing method nodes and derivation/adaptation edges (method lineage view).
A timeline view that overlays key method introductions and major forks/evolutions.
A Sankey or flow diagram illustrating how components (e.g., architectures, loss functions, datasets) combine and diverge across papers.
A mockup of an interactive explorer UI (search + path-finding between methods + API call examples).
paper_title: Intern-Atlas: A Methodological Evolution Graph as Research Infrastructure for AI Scientists
paper_authors: Yujun Wu, Dongxu Zhang, Xinchen Li, Jinhang Xu, Yiling Duan
